The first author of the report, Richard Murphy, claims that the fastest growing sector in the US economy – fast food – has, for years, been paying the least while raking-in enormous profits. The second report by the UNISON, which is Britain’s largest and oldest trade union, claims that the living wage movement is making real progress in Britain and the US. The problem, as Murphy puts it in his report, is that these workers are paid a low wage.

North Carolina coach Sylvia Hatchell said her team is playing better basketball.
"But we haven't peaked," she said.
Hatchell's No. 8 Lady Wolfpack, who are in an eight-way logjam in the ACC's Atlantic Division, led wire-to-wire Monday as they remained unbeaten this season with a 75-49 rout of Virginia in Charlottesville, Va.
Hatchell said her team's last few games have shown it has improved since the start of the season. She believes the NCAA Tournament, which begins Friday in San Antonio, Texas, will be telling.
"It will be a good measuring stick," she said. "From what I see, we are playing better. If we peak at the right time, we can compete for a championship."

. Not everyone listens. Not everyone does what is recommended. Not everyone takes their medication. And still, here we are.

in his right shoulder in May, Winker sought a third opinion from Dr. Neal ElAttrache of Kerlan-Jobe in Los Angeles. The diagnosis from Dr. ElAttrache was that Winker will undergo season-ending surgery to repair a tear in his labrum.
Winker was batting .299 this year with 7 homers and 43 RBI in 105 games.
The Reds placed Winker on the 60-day injured list. He will undergo surgery and is expected to miss six to eight months.
In his place, Aristides Aquino will take over as Cincinnati’s primary left fielder. Right-handed pitcher Matt Bowman will join the Reds’ 30-man active roster.

the $1.5 trillion Senate tax bill that passed out of the Finance Committee late last week. The next step is for the Senate to hold a floor vote before the chamber leaves town for the holidays.
So what is the rush, you might ask, to get this done so quickly?
Let’s take a look.
You may remember that the House of Representatives already passed its own version of the bill, which the Senate then had to amend and pass its own version of to meet the 60-vote (and likely some other) requirement it faces in the upper chamber.
So now the two chambers are in conference, trying to come to consensus on an agreement they hope they can agree upon before the start of the next “regular session” on Jan. 19, 2017. The sooner they can agree to it, the sooner they can send it to the President for his signature.
Let’s assume it does get signed before the end of the year.

company. I don't want to spend the whole day in the kitchen, or have to make one more thing before tucking my guests in for the night.

So I'm thrilled to present my favorite Thanksgiving recipe: the Pumpkin Cheesecake Bars. You can make this cheesecake ahead of time, and it freezes beautifully. After it thaws, you can slice it and serve it. No one will guess that the filling and crust were made ahead. A bonus is that the bars can be made up to three days in advance. You'll be glad you did.

You need:

4 large graham cracker squares (1 package)

1/3 C all-purpose flour

2/3 C sugar

2/3 C cream cheese, softened

2 Tbsp. melted butter

2/3 C sour cream

1/3 C confectioners' sugar

2 Tbsp. vanilla extract

fresh cran
